subject: Re: MSA + On-Prem Addendum — license entitlements & audit window
messages:

Subject: MSA + On-Prem addendum — initial redlines and questions

Alex / David — attaching our consolidated redlines for the MSA and the On-Prem addendum (files attached). We flagged the items we need explicit confirmation on so we can move to procurement: 

1) License grant boundary — we need to confirm the customer can run a copy of the model binaries in our VPC and in an on-prem air-gapped cluster. Please confirm whether Redwood will permit that or requires an operator-handback process.

2) Audit & evidence — Crestline needs an auditable, notarized proof of access process (we proposed an escrow-like sealed snapshot). If Redwood has an equivalent (witnessed snapshot + hash attestations), outline the workflow and who is the steward.

3) Operator access & credentials — what minimal operator role is required for Redwood (if any) for troubleshooting? We need exact limits (no remote shell, read-only logs, ACLs).

4) Retention & FOR (forensic) access — retention periods and whether forensic snapshots can be exported to our secure archive.

5) Timeline — procurement is targeting week of Mar 13 for signatures; can Redwood confirm a legal sync this week to resolve open redlines?

Attached: Crestline_Redlines_MSA_20280301.docx, OnPrem_Addendum_redline.pdf

Happy to set a call — Priya (cc) will coordinate.

Thanks,
Evan Liu
Sr. Contracts Manager
Crestline Therapeutics

From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: MSA + On-Prem addendum — initial redlines and questions

Hi Evan — thanks for the clear redlines, and welcome Priya. Alex from Redwood here — I’ve looped in Lauren from Legal and Marissa (Ops/Deploy) to cover the operator and evidence pieces. Quick notes from our side to unblock procurement: 

- License boundary: Redwood’s standard approach is to grant a non-exclusive, non-transferable license to run the model in Customer-controlled environments (VPCs or on-prem hardware) — we can tighten the language to "Customer-controlled VPC and Customer-operated on-prem cluster". We will not permit sublicensing; we will allow dev/staging copies within the same account.

- Evidence / escrow alternative: Redwood prefers a witnessed, sealed-snapshot workflow over third-party escrow in many cases. That would be: Redwood generates a platform snapshot, we perform a joint witness session (remote or on-site), produce a tamper-evident hash, and deliver the sealed artifact to Crestline's secure drive. That process is auditable and avoids full code escrow. We can document the witness steps in an exhibit.

- Audit window: we can offer a standard remote audit window (48 continuous hours with read-only console traces and streamed logs). For on-site forensic access we typically require advance notice and a scoped limited access period; we can propose a 3-day notice window in the addendum.

- Operator access: we will propose explicit operator roles that allow support to triage (read-only logs + metrics, no inbound shell by default). If Crestline requires emergency write-level access, that requires a separate authorization flow with a 2-person approval and ephemeral keys.

Proposed next step: legal + ops sync early next week. I’m available Fri 11am PT or Mon 9am PT. Lauren — would you prefer to draft clause language for §3 (License), §7 (Audit), and an exhibit describing the witness/sequence?

—Alex
Alex Martinez
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: evidence_matrix.xlsx (ops input)
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Evan Liu <evan.liu@crestline.com>, Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
Cc: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 1 Mar 2028 14:33:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MSA + On-Prem addendum — proposed clause language

Evan / Alex / team — I reviewed the redlines and drafted targeted clause suggestions to keep execution velocity while protecting Redwood IP and limiting operational exposure. Sending high-level suggestions and an editable doc (Clause_Requests_v3.docx). Key points below: 

1) License Grant (proposed wording): "Subject to Customer's compliance, Redwood grants Customer a limited, non-exclusive, non-sublicensable license to use Provider software and model artifacts solely within Customer-controlled infrastructure (defined as Customer VPCs and Customer-operated premises)." This preserves the on-prem right while preventing uncontrolled redistribution.

2) Operator Roles & Escalation: define "Operator Role" as a set of read-only telemetry + metrics and a separate "Emergency Support Role" that requires documented approval from named Crestline admins and is logged and time-limited. We suggest language that requires Redwood to provide an access report after any emergency session.

3) Evidence/Witnessing Exhibit: instead of handing full source code to an escrow agent, the Exhibit will define a sealed-snapshot & witness routine: generation, joint witness session (remote video + hash), secure transfer, and retention period (90 days mirrored in Crestline archive). If Crestline insists on escrow, propose a narrow escrow scope: snapshot only (no operator keys).

4) Audit mechanics: remote audits permitted with 48-hour window; on-site audits are limited to material contract disputes and require 3 business days' notice with mutually agreed scope.

5) Data & Forensics: Redwood will provide encrypted forensic exports upon lawful request and per the exhibit's retention schedule; retention exceptions require a separate data transfer agreement.

If Crestline can confirm they are comfortable with the sealed-snapshot + witness flow, we can incorporate the exhibit and close the outstanding items rapidly. I’ll attach Clause_Requests_v3.docx with tracked language for §3 and §7.

Lauren Bishop
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Attachments: Clause_Requests_v3.docx (draft clause language)

Lauren / Alex — thanks for the quick turnaround and for the concrete exhibit idea. Crestline legal is broadly comfortable with the sealed-snapshot + witness approach as an alternative to a full escrow deposit, subject to two asks: 

1) Notarized witness & tamper-evident proof: Can Redwood provide a third-party timestamp / notarization on the produced hash (we use that as evidence in procurement audits)?

2) Transport & retention: We need the artifact to be exported in an encrypted container (S3 or physical) that Crestline can hold in our evidence vault. Please confirm retention period (90 days ok) and the process for extension.

If Redwood agrees to the above, we can accept the exhibit and proceed. Bryn (counsel) wants to run a quick redline call — is Mon Mar 5, 10:00 AM PT workable for Redwood legal + ops? Priya will Doodle if that time doesn't work.

I attached a small inline-comment version of the addendum redline that calls out the witnesses and transport language.

Evan Liu
Sr. Contracts Manager, Crestline Therapeutics
